name: Silver Jews
label: Drag City
lede: Two museum guards and a college friend taping noise in Hoboken became the vehicle for David Berman's songs, sung by a poet who wouldn't tour until 2006 and ended the band 333 feet underground.

eras.title: Noise from a Hoboken living room
eras.text: David Berman met Stephen Malkmus and Bob Nastanovich at the University of Virginia, and the three started taping deliberately bad music in a Hoboken apartment. It began as an art joke. Then Pavement took off, and Silver Jews became the place Berman's writing lived.

years.h: David Berman arrives at the University of Virginia
years.p: Williamsburg, Virginia native David Berman starts at UVA, where he meets future [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]] members Stephen Malkmus and Bob Nastanovich. He graduates in 1989 with an English degree.

years.h: Silver Jews start in a Hoboken living room
years.p: David Berman, Stephen Malkmus and Bob Nastanovich record noisy demos in their Hoboken, New Jersey apartment. Berman later joked the name came from a Silver Jewelry billboard.
years.xp: The name started as a conceptual-art pseudonym, and it stuck.

years.h: David Berman and Stephen Malkmus guard the Whitney
years.p: In the early 1990s David Berman and Stephen Malkmus work as security guards at New York's Whitney Museum of American Art. Berman said the art on the walls fed his lyrics.

years.h: The Arizona Record, the last of the lo-fi EPs
years.p: Drag City issues The Arizona Record, the EP that closes out Silver Jews' home-taped early years. The early singles and EPs were later gathered on Early Times (2012).

eras.title: Pavement's side project, Berman's whole life
eras.text: In the mid-90s Silver Jews were filed as a Pavement offshoot, since Malkmus and Nastanovich kept showing up. But the songs were Berman's, and by American Water Pitchfork was handing him a 9.9.

years.h: Starlite Walker: the first real album, cut in Memphis
years.p: Recorded in June 1994 at Easley Recordings in Memphis with Davis McCain and Doug Easley, the first Silver Jews album still has Stephen Malkmus and Bob Nastanovich aboard. Berman said Trains Across the Sea was his first original song.
years.xp: Berman said the idea was a record that looked like a real record, with song titles and everything, full of the songs the Whitney guards made at home that sounded terrible.

years.h: The Natural Bridge, without Stephen Malkmus
years.p: David Berman makes the second Silver Jews album without Pavement's Stephen Malkmus.

years.h: American Water: Malkmus returns, Pitchfork gives it 9.9
years.p: Cut at the Rare Book Room in Brooklyn with Stephen Malkmus back on guitar and vocals, American Water gets a 9.9 from Pitchfork. It opens with Random Rules; Smith & Jones Forever is track two.
years.xp:
Mike Fellows played bass, Tim Barnes drums, Chris Stroffolino keys and trumpet. The working title was The Late, Great Silver Jews, a nod to Townes Van Zandt's The Late Great Townes Van Zandt.

Pitchfork later ranked the album No. 21 of the 1990s.

years.h: David Berman's poetry book Actual Air
years.p: Open City Books publishes David Berman's poetry collection Actual Air, which sells over 20,000 copies, a rare number for poetry.

years.h: David Berman marries Cassie
years.p: David Berman marries Cassie, whom he'd met at a party two years before. He called her the best thing that ever happened to him.

eras.title: Nashville, and nearly the end
eras.text: Berman moved to Nashville, brought Cassie into the band, and went through the worst years of his life on the way to Tanglewood Numbers: crack, a suicide attempt, rehab his estranged father paid for, and a turn to Judaism.

years.h: Bright Flight: Cassie Berman joins the band
years.p: The first Silver Jews album made in Nashville brings in Cassie Berman on vocals, William Tyler on guitar and Tony Crow on keys.

years.h: David Berman's suicide attempt in Nashville
years.p: Per Wikipedia, David Berman took crack cocaine, alcohol and tranquilizers intending to die. Cassie Berman found him; he woke at Vanderbilt University Medical Center three days later.
years.xp: Berman had been using hard drugs since 1998. He went to rehab afterward, paid for by his father, and said he had not used heroin or cocaine since October 2003. In recovery he took up Judaism and studied the Torah; he later said the faith lasted from 2004 to 2010.

years.h: Tanglewood Numbers: Malkmus, Nastanovich and Will Oldham
years.p: The comeback album reunites Stephen Malkmus and Bob Nastanovich with David Berman and adds [[Will Oldham|eb51090c-662a-47a1-967c-c63292d9831a]]. William Eggleston's photograph is on the cover.
years.xp: The album nearly didn't make it: the Easley-McCain studio in Memphis, where Silver Jews had cut Starlite Walker and where mastering was set, burned down. The tapes survived.

eras.title: Finally on stage, then gone
eras.text: For their first seventeen years Silver Jews barely played live. Sober and newly religious, Berman took the band around the world, including Israel, then shut it down with a public letter about his father and one last show in a cave.

years.h: Silver Jews' first-ever tour
years.p: After years of avoiding the stage, Silver Jews tour North America and Europe behind Tanglewood Numbers, with Brian Kotzur on drums.

years.h: Two shows in Tel Aviv, filmed as Silver Jew
years.p: Silver Jews play two shows in Tel Aviv and visit Jerusalem. Michael Tully films it in three days with no budget; Drag City releases Silver Jew on DVD in September 2008.

years.h: Lookout Mountain, Lookout Sea, the last Silver Jews album
years.p: The sixth and final Silver Jews studio album.

q: I always said we would stop before we got bad.
years.h: David Berman ends Silver Jews and names his father
years.p: On Drag City's message board, David Berman retires Silver Jews and reveals his father is lobbyist Richard Berman, saying the band was too small a force to undo his harm.
years.xp:
Berman had been estranged from his father since around 2006. Richard Berman was a Washington lobbyist for the firearms and alcohol industries, among others; this was the first time David named him in public.

He also joked that if he kept recording he might accidentally write the answer song to R.E.M.'s Shiny Happy People, and said he wanted to try screenwriting or muckraking.

years.h: The last show: 333 feet underground in a Tennessee cave
years.p: Silver Jews play their final show at Cumberland Caverns in McMinnville, Tennessee, 333 feet below ground, for 300 general-admission tickets. The last song is Smith & Jones Forever.

eras.title: Purple Mountains
eras.text: A decade after the cave show, Berman came back under a new name with a record about grief and his broken marriage. A month later he was dead.

years.h: Early Times collects the early EPs
years.p: Drag City gathers the lo-fi Silver Jews singles and EPs, including The Arizona Record, on one album.

years.h: A Silver Jews reunion photo turns out to be a prank
years.p: A Facebook photo hinting at a reunion gets fans going; it was a joke.

years.h: David and Cassie Berman separate
years.p: After 19 years together in Nashville, David and Cassie Berman separate.

years.h: Purple Mountains: David Berman's first album in 11 years
years.p: David Berman returns with Purple Mountains on Drag City, made with members of Woods. It's hailed as an unexpected second act.
years.xp: Promoting it, Berman said there had been around 100 nights in the last ten years when he was sure he wouldn't make it to morning.

years.h: David Berman dies at 52
years.p: David Berman died by suicide, by hanging, at an apartment in Park Slope, Brooklyn, a month after Purple Mountains came out, according to Wikipedia. He was 52.
